points.title: so/such…that… 如此...以致... (結果副詞子句)
examples: It was on this day that the United States became independent.
It was Jason that won first place in the English speech contest.
It was in the French restaurant that I lost my wallet.
Gary is so tired that he can’t focus on the exam now.
Math is such a difficult subject that most students don’t like it.

items.sentence: It *was* October 28, 1886.
Even though it was a rainy day in New York City, close to a million people *were* out for their first look at the city’s newest addition on Bedloe’s Island, which was later renamed Liberty Island.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (Even though...) + S + Vi + Relative clause (which...)

items.sentence: When French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi removed the large French flag from the front of his latest creation, the crowds *cheered* and the soldiers *fired* their guns in celebration.
The grand sight before their eyes *was* the Statue of Liberty.
The Statue of Liberty *is* a gift that France presented to America to celebrate its one hundred years of independence from Great Britain.
The full height of the monument *is* 305 feet, and the statue itself *stands* 151 feet tall.
When it was first created, the statue’s copper surface *was* reddish-brown.
Over time, this outer layer *has been exposed* to the air and *oxidized* so much that it has turned green.
items.pattern: S + Vi (Passive / Compound verb) + Result clause (so... that...)

items.sentence: Each part of the statue *has* a special meaning.
In her left hand, Lady Liberty *holds* a giant tablet with the date “July 4, 1776” on it.
It *was* on this day that the United States became independent, and the tablet *symbolizes* a new and free America.
items.pattern: It-Cleft sentence (It was... that...) + Compound sentence (with "and")

items.sentence: A giant torch, which symbolizes that Lady Liberty lights the way to freedom, *is held* firmly in her right hand.
items.pattern: S + Relative clause (which... with inner Noun clause) + Vi (Passive)

items.sentence: Other symbolic parts of the statue *include* Lady Liberty’s crown, her dress, and the broken chains at her feet.
Seven spikes *rise* from the top of the crown and *represent* the rays of the sun.
Lady Liberty *is* thus divine and *shines* her heavenly light on the world.
items.pattern: S + Vl/Vt (Compound verb with adjective C and object)

items.sentence: Her robe in the ancient Roman style *shows* that Bartholdi was also inspired by Libertas, the Roman goddess of freedom.
The broken chains *represent* the end of slavery in the United States and *symbolize* freedom from unfair treatment.
Today, the Statue of Liberty *is* one of America’s biggest tourist attractions.
It *is* such a popular landmark that every visitor to New York City has heard of it and wants to pay a visit.
items.pattern: S + Vl + C + Result clause (such... that...)

items.sentence: As always, Lady Liberty *stands* tall and proud.
items.pattern: Adverbial phrase + S + Vl + C (Subject complements)

items.sentence: She *has* now *become* a symbol of hope and freedom for visitors from around the globe.

text_genre.raw_text: This is a descriptive text that tells readers about the history and symbol of the Statue of Liberty.  Through reading the text, readers can get relevant information regarding the Statue of Liberty. It follows the structure of: the opening & introduction, meaning of each part of the statue, and the conclusion.
